open_slices_in_flight.root_cause: Two distinct signatures: (1) original `tokio::time::sleep(2s)` not enough under tarpaulin-instrumented CI runners — replaced by `wait_for_first_event` bounded poll on probe_drain_log with observable exit criterion (events.length > 0). (2) `cursor remains identical` on second drain — NOT a server-side probe_drain bug; cursor staying identical is CORRECT behaviour when the log has produced no new records between drains. The fixture's test_busyloop generates events at a rate the first drain consumes in one pass, so by the time the second drain runs, there are no new records. Fix: `wait_for_log_advance` bounded poll on probe_drain (not probe_drain_log) with exit criterion total_buffered > first_total, 5s deadline.
open_slices_in_flight.tests_passing: uat_c2_01 + uat_c2_02 + uat_c2_03 + diagnostic: 4/4 green. multi_session (CIH-F surface): 7/7.
open_slices_in_flight.no_assertion_change: line 114 cursor-advances contract untouched; only the precondition that the log must have advanced between drains is now met by an observable bounded poll instead of a fixed sleep.
open_slices_in_flight.no_blind_waits: both helpers poll observable signals with hard deadlines and panic with actionable diagnostics on timeout

fix_2.supersedes_claim: v1 claimed total_buffered was the monotonic log-advance signal; it is not — it is the count of raw events in the page.
fix_2.root_cause_of_fix_2: GH Actions Coverage run 35471023325 at b98b747f failed uat_c2_01 with 'did not produce any new records within 5000ms after the first drain (first_total=19...)'. CI tarpaulin instrumentation makes the fixture produce events much more slowly than local (~19 events vs 270+); with limit=1000 the first drain takes everything the fixture has at that point, the log then drains the rest of the 3s busyloop window into the file while no drain is observing it, and after the first drain finishes `total_buffered > 19` on a same-size page is false (total_buffered is `events.len()` of THIS page, not a log total — see canonical_drain.rs:299).
fix_2.fix: Two coordinated changes, no assertion change: (1) first drain uses limit=1 + call_tool (not probe_drain_with_evidence_cursor which hardcodes limit=1000) so it cannot consume the entire output; the drain logic pairs each requested Raw with its derived TripwireFired records (canonical_drain.rs logical-boundary check), so even limit=1 returns the Raw plus its firing records. (2) wait_for_log_advance compares cursor STRINGS, not total_buffered; the canonical ECV1 token includes the seq in its last segment, so a different token means new records were examined. Still bounded (5s deadline = 2x the fixture's 3s runtime), still observable (cursor's encoded seq is the canonical evidence of forward progress), still no blind sleep.

fix_3.root_cause_of_fix_3: GH Actions Coverage run 35472264098 at fd9dae9e failed uat_c2_01 with 'first_event_after_ms=5078 deadline_ms=5000' and 'first_drain events=0 total_buffered=0 cursor=...:0'. CI tarpaulin instrumentation on a stressed runner takes 6-8x longer for the fixture's test_busyloop to produce its first event than the fixture's claimed 3s runtime; 5s is not enough margin. The previous v2 code continued past wait_for_first_event even when count=0, leaving an empty log and producing a `cursor stays at seq=0` no-op.
fix_3.fix: Two coordinated changes: (1) bail with an actionable diagnostic when wait_for_first_event returns count=0 — the contract under test is vacuous against an empty log. The bail-out message names the three plausible root causes (fixture did not start, subscription not wired to the same session, tarpaulin-instrumented busyloop too slow) and re-emits the probe_drain wire shape. (2) Increase UAT_C2_01_FIRST_EVENT_DEADLINE and UAT_C2_01_LOG_ADVANCE_DEADLINE from 5s to 10s — 2x the worst observed CI time, still a hard cap (no blind sleep).
fix_3.tests_passing_post_fix_3: 4/4 rec_c2_2_uat_c2 locally. log_advance_ms grew to 112ms locally because limit=1 leaves a smaller head start for the next probe, but the test completes in ~21s with the 10s deadline upper bound.

slices_executed.title: UAT-C2-01 root cause: bounded poll for log advance + diagnostic
slices_executed.rationale: Two distinct UAT-C2-01 failures under tarpaulin-instrumented CI runners. (1) Original tokio::time::sleep(2s) not always enough — wait_for_first_event replaces it (bounded poll on probe_drain_log with criterion events.length > 0, 5s deadline). (2) cursor remains identical on second drain — NOT a server-side probe_drain bug; the cursor staying identical is the CORRECT behaviour when the log has produced no new records between drains. Reproduced locally: first_drain total_buffered=270 cursor=ecv1:...:405, second drain reads from seq=405 with nothing new, encodes back to ecv1:...:405. The contract under test ('an examined page must advance the cursor') necessarily requires new records between drains; the previous setup assumed wall-clock would produce them. wait_for_log_advance — bounded poll on probe_drain (NOT probe_drain_log, so we hit the same handler and read total_buffered which is the only signal that says the log has new records without consuming them). Exit criterion total_buffered > first_total. 5s deadline matches busyloop's claimed runtime x 2. No assertion change: line 114 cursor-advances contract is untouched. No blind waits: both helpers poll observable signals with hard deadlines and panic with actionable diagnostics on timeout.
